title: Rehearse the native governance MCP journey in a real Codex host

requirement.summary: Install the reviewed create-missing-only project MCP configuration and record one live, uncoached Codex rehearsal of the five-tool alignment and active-Agent self-review journey without manually directing tool calls.

objective.rationale: Offline protocol tests prove deterministic boundaries but not whether a production Codex host discovers and selects the tools at the right moments while preserving human direction ownership.

goal: Obtain honest live-host evidence for tool discovery, selection timing, human-owned alignment, current-Agent self-review, privacy, authority, and interaction burden, then record observed failures without weakening the contracts.
non_goals: Do not coach Codex to call a named MCP tool or hand-author protocol payloads during the measured journey.
Do not change the five-tool Core contract, add a model SDK or credential, start a second Agent, or implement an independent Reviewer.
Do not treat one Codex rehearsal as proof for Claude Code, IDE hosts, general semantic correctness, causal benefit, or production readiness.
Do not overwrite or merge existing Codex configuration, bypass project trust review, or preserve raw prompts, transcripts, source, credentials, or absolute host paths as governance evidence.
Do not commit, push, publish, release, deploy, or mutate a consumer repository.
acceptance_signals: The reviewed integration plan creates only a previously missing .codex/config.toml after explicit human authorization and preserves Codex trusted-project review as a separate decision.
A fresh real Codex host discovers the AgentGov MCP server and its exact five tools without source-path or hand-authored protocol setup.
One ordinary ambiguous request causes Codex to use alignment tools at appropriate moments, ask the human for direction, and record only the human-selected resolution.
After the bounded work, the same active Codex Agent invokes the medium-risk self-review tools and returns advisory observations without claiming independent assurance or downstream authority.
The record distinguishes observed facts, advisory interpretation, failures, coaching, restarts, privacy exposure, and unknowns; any manual tool direction disqualifies the run as uncoached evidence.
The rehearsal performs no Git write, publication, release, deployment, consumer mutation, external Provider call, or hidden background execution.
Task, scope, repository, documentation, and diff validation pass for the recorded result.

items: A production model may ignore, misuse, or overuse the tools even though the protocol is correct.
Calling the rehearsal uncoached after manual tool direction would overstate evidence.
Project configuration is executable and requires separate Codex trust review.
A live transcript may contain private content and must not be copied into retained governance evidence.

stop_conditions: Stop if .codex/config.toml already exists or the integration requires overwrite, merge, or trust bypass.
Stop if the measured journey requires coaching a named tool, hand-authored MCP payloads, raw transcript retention, a credential, network setup, or another Agent.
Stop if Codex selects the user's direction, claims independent assurance, or gains task, Git, release, deployment, or external-write authority.
Stop before Git writes, publication, release, deployment, consumer mutation, or a second-host proof.

decision.rationale: The live rehearsal produced an honest failed product result: tool discovery and selection worked, but generic Core rejection blocked human alignment and self-review. The user explicitly authorized the recommended diagnostic correction on 2026-08-06; this rehearsal is paused for routing hygiene without claiming success.
